name: Oatmeal Man
approach: From US Highway 2 at milepost 42 in the town of Baring (directly across from Der Baring Store), turn north onto Barclay Creek Road, Forest Service Road 6024, cross the BNSF railroad tracks and bear left at the fork about 0.2 miles up. Follow FS 6024 roughly 4.3–4.5 miles of gravel to the Barclay Lake trailhead at about 2,280 ft, where there is parking for roughly 20 cars, a vault toilet and picnic tables but no potable water. Walk Barclay Creek Trail 1055 east up the valley — it is a gentle, well-graded 2.2 miles to Barclay Lake at about 2,420 ft, directly under the wall. The north face rises straight out of the lake basin: 3,703 vertical feet from the lake to the summit in only half a mile of horizontal distance. Leave the trail near the lake and fight up the steep forested and brushy hillside beneath the wall — the first ascent of this face in 1961 found the first 1,000 feet to be exactly that kind of brush-and-forest struggle to reach a camp below the couloirs, and nothing about that terrain has improved since. There is no maintained climbers' path to the base of the main-peak wall (the fixed lines and boot track that exist on this mountain belong to the Dolomite Tower approach, which breaks off the trail well before the lake and heads up a different drainage). Allow several hours from the car to the base and expect wet vegetation, blowdown and loose ground.

approach_variants.name: Barclay Creek Trail 1055 to the lake, then straight up the north face hillside
approach_variants.notes:
From US-2 at milepost 42 in Baring, directly across from the store, turn north onto Barclay Creek Road (FR 6024), cross the BNSF tracks and bear left at the fork about 0.2 miles up. Follow about 4.3 to 4.5 miles of gravel to the Barclay Lake trailhead at roughly 2,280 ft — parking for about 20 cars, a vault toilet, picnic tables, no potable water.

Unlike the ridge and face routes, this one uses the maintained trail: Barclay Creek Trail 1055 runs gently east up the valley about 2.2 miles to Barclay Lake at around 2,420 ft, directly beneath the wall. The north face rises roughly 3,700 vertical feet from the lake in only half a mile of horizontal distance.

Leave the trail near the lake and climb the steep forested, brushy hillside beneath the wall. The 1961 first-ascent account of this face describes the first 1,000 ft as exactly that — a brush-and-forest struggle to reach a camp below the couloirs — and nothing about that terrain has improved. Allow several hours from the car to the base.
hazards: Pathless steep brush and blowdown for the first 1,000 ft
No fixed protection or path — retreat is by the same brush
Easy to end up on the Dolomite Tower approach in the wrong drainage
approach_variants.baseFinding: There is no maintained climbers' path to the main-peak wall, and that absence is itself the navigation aid. The fixed lines, hand lines and boot track that exist on this mountain belong to the Dolomite Tower approach, which leaves the trail well before the lake and goes up a different drainage. If you find fixed rope, bolted slab or a worn boot track on your way to the base, you are in the wrong drainage entirely — turn around and go back to the lake. The correct ground is pathless: wet vegetation, blowdown and loose forest floor, gained by leaving the trail at the lake and going straight up.

pitch_detail.notes: Roughly 1,000 ft of steep forested and brushy hillside from near Barclay Lake up to the couloir/ledge system at the toe of the wall. This is the same ground the 1960 first-ascent party fixed lines on; it is part of the climb, not a trail.

About fourteen pitches of mixed free climbing on the 2,600-ft north face, reported by Peter Doorish as 5.11c overall. No published pitch-by-pitch topo exists — the first-ascent note gives only the grade, the pitch count and the face height, so individual pitch lengths and cruxes are undocumented. Expect sustained 5.10 with 5.11 cruxes on gneiss of variable quality, interrupted by ledge and vegetation bands.
Easy scrambling from the top of the wall along the summit ridge to the true north summit at 6,127 ft.

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 2 in Baring, directly across from the store, turn north onto 635th Place NE, cross the railroad tracks and keep left at the junction about 0.3 mile up, where the road becomes FS Road 6024. Follow the potholed gravel about 4 more miles to the Barclay Lake trailhead, with parking for about 20 cars and a vault toilet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.
